body:
You've found the perfect crib. It looks beautiful in your nursery, fits your space, and checks all the boxes. Now comes a decision that might be even more important: choosing the right crib mattress.

Unlike an adult mattress, where comfort often means softness, the best crib mattress for a baby needs to be firm, flat, and fit properly inside the crib. And with so many options promising everything from breathability to organic materials, it's not always easy to know which features actually matter.

Whether you're shopping for your first baby or upgrading your nursery, here's what to look for in a crib mattress, which features are worth paying attention to, and why we're excited to welcome Moonlight to the dadadababy family.

1. Firmness Comes First

When choosing a mattress for yourself, you might look for something soft and plush. For a newborn, it's the opposite.

The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends placing babies on a firm, flat, non-inclined sleep surface. A mattress that's too soft can conform to a baby's face or body, increasing the risk of suffocation.

A good infant crib mattress should maintain its shape rather than creating a deep indentation when pressure is applied. That's why mattresses specifically designed for infant sleep are different from the mattresses older children and adults use.

Some crib mattresses, including Moonlight's Little Dreamer, offer two different firmness levels: an extra-firm side for infants and a slightly softer side for toddlers. This can be a practical choice for parents who want a mattress that continues to serve their child as they grow.

2. Make Sure the Mattress Fits Your Crib

Even a high-quality mattress isn't the right choice if it doesn't fit your crib properly.

A crib mattress should sit flat and fit snugly inside the crib, without dangerous gaps around the edges where a baby could become trapped. Always check the mattress dimensions against your crib manufacturer's instructions and confirm that the two products are compatible.

Most standard full-size cribs are designed for standard crib mattresses, but that doesn't mean you should skip the fit check, especially if you have a mini crib or a model with different mattress requirements.

For example, the Moonlight Little Dreamer Crib Mattress measures 27.5 inches by 52 inches and is 5 inches thick. It's designed for standard U.S. cribs, including a snug fit in dadada baby's Soho crib.

Before buying any crib and mattress combination, confirm compatibility with the exact models you've selected. A snug, secure fit matters far more than matching the brand names.

3. Look for Waterproof, Easy-to-Clean Materials

Here's something every new parent learns pretty quickly: babies are messy sleepers.

Between diaper leaks, spit-up, and unexpected middle-of-the-night changes, your baby's mattress will probably need cleaning more often than you expect.

A waterproof crib mattress can make those moments a lot easier. Instead of worrying about moisture getting into the mattress core, you can clean the surface according to the manufacturer's instructions.

Look for a cover that's easy to wipe down, resists stains, and doesn't require a complicated cleaning routine. Some mattresses come with removable covers, while others have a built-in waterproof surface.

Moonlight's Little Dreamer features a waterproof, medical-grade performance fabric cover designed to resist stains and odors. It can be cleaned with a damp sponge and mild soap, making everyday upkeep simple.

If you choose to use a separate mattress protector, make sure it's thin, tightly fitted, and compatible with your mattress. Avoid anything that adds soft padding or interferes with the mattress's intended firmness and fit.

4. Understand What Mattress Certifications Actually Mean

You'll probably notice terms like GREENGUARD Gold, CertiPUR-US, and low VOC while shopping for crib mattresses. They can be helpful, but it's worth understanding what they tell you.

GREENGUARD Gold certification means a product has been tested against standards for low chemical emissions, including volatile organic compounds (VOCs), which can affect indoor air quality.

CertiPUR-US certification applies specifically to polyurethane foam. It verifies that the foam meets certain standards for chemical content, emissions, and durability.

The Moonlight Little Dreamer is GREENGUARD Gold certified and contains CertiPUR-US certified foam. It also uses a fiberglass-free woven fire barrier without spray-on fire-retardant chemicals.

These are useful details for parents who care about the materials they bring into their nursery. However, certifications for chemical emissions don't replace the need to check mattress firmness, compatibility, and compliance with applicable crib mattress safety standards.

5. Consider a Mattress That Grows With Your Baby

Babies grow quickly, and many parents want nursery furniture that won't need replacing after the first year.

That's one reason dual-sided crib mattresses have become a popular option. They're designed with different sleep surfaces for different developmental stages, so parents can continue using the mattress as their child gets older.

With the Little Dreamer, the extra-firm side is intended for infants, while the other side provides firm support for toddlers. Moonlight instructs parents to use the infant side for at least the first 12 months and to follow the product's guidance before switching sides.

Of course, a dual-sided mattress isn't a requirement. A properly fitted, appropriately firm crib mattress can also serve a growing child. The important thing is choosing something that meets your child's needs at each stage.

Introducing Moonlight's Little Dreamer: Now at dadadababy

  • Waterproof performance cover: Designed for easy cleaning and everyday messes.

We're especially excited to offer families another way to complete their nursery alongside our collection of convertible cribs.

6. Don't Forget About Safe Sleep Basics

Choosing a good crib mattress is important, but how you use it matters just as much.

According to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission and the American Academy of Pediatrics, babies should be placed on their backs for sleep, on a firm, flat mattress with a properly fitted sheet.

Keep the crib free of pillows, loose blankets, bumpers, stuffed animals, and additional padding. Even if a mattress is marketed as breathable, that doesn't change established safe-sleep recommendations.

It's also worth setting up your crib and mattress well before your baby's arrival. Inspect the mattress when it arrives, make sure it fits properly, and allow any compressed mattress to expand fully according to the manufacturer's instructions.

For the Moonlight Little Dreamer, the mattress ships compressed and rolled and may take three to five days to reach its full shape. The crib and mattress may also arrive separately, so it's smart to leave extra time before your due date.

How to Choose the Best Crib Mattress for Your Family

There's no single crib mattress that's perfect for every nursery. Your choice will depend on your crib, your budget, the materials you prefer, and the features that make everyday life easier.

But the priorities are straightforward: start with safety, confirm the fit, and look for practical features you'll appreciate after your baby arrives.

A waterproof cover might not seem particularly exciting when you're designing a beautiful nursery, but at 2 a.m., you'll probably be grateful for it. And a dual-sided mattress may be worth considering if you're hoping to use the same sleep setup into the toddler years.

With our new Moonlight partnership, dadadababy is making it easier to explore another thoughtfully designed mattress option while shopping for your baby's crib.

Because the best nursery purchases aren't necessarily the ones with the longest feature lists. They're the ones that make sense for your family, work well together, and help you feel prepared for what's ahead.
